div.head: Had 2[as Að]
div.ab: Be gehadodra manna aðe; ⁊ be hadbote. Mæssepreostes að ⁊ worldþegnes is on Engla lage geteald efen dire for ðam seofon cirichadan, þe se preost þurh Godes gife geþéah, þæt he hæfde.
Be gehádendra áðe; ⁊ be hádbote. Mæssepreostes áð ⁊ woruldþegenes is on Engla lage geteald éfen dýre for þam seofon cirichádon, þe se preost þurh Godes gife geþéah, þæt he hæfde.
Mæssepreostes að ⁊ woruldþegenes is on Engla lage geteald efen dyre; ⁊ for þam seofon cyrichadan, þe se mæssepreost þurh Godes gife geþeah, þæt he hæfde, he bið þegenrihtes wyrþe.
Messepreostes ⁊ weoroldðegnes aþ on Engla laga biþ gelic gedemod; and for þam seofon cyriclicum endebyrdnyssum, ðam se preost be Godes gyfa up astiged, biþ he þæs ðegnes rihtes geweorþod.

Misse presbiteri et secularis thaini iusiurandum in Anglorum lege computatur (reputatur) eque carum; et pro septem ordinibus ecclesię, quo sacerdos per Dei donum ascendit, ut haberet, thaini recto (rectitudine) dignus est.
[45] Sacramentum presbiteri regulariter uiuentis tantundem ualet (scilicet) sicut liberalis hominis, propter septem ęcclesiasticos ordines.

Be gehadodra manna aðe Mæssepreostes að and worldþegenes is on Engla lage geteald efen dyre; and for ðam seofon cirichadan, þe se mæssepreost þurh Godes gife geþeah, þæt he hæfde, he bið þegenrihtes wyrþe.

(Vom Eide geweihter Männer; und von Clerusbusse DO) Der Eid eines Priesters und [der] eines weltlichen Thegn wird im Engländer-Recht gleich werthvoll gerechnet wegen der 7 kirchlichen Weihen, die zu erhalten der Priester durch Gottes Gnade das Glück hatte (gerechnet; und wegen — — hatte, ist er Thegn-Privilegs würdig [gewürdigt Ld] hlq).

(Of the oath of ordained men; and of compensation for clergy, DO) The oath of a mass-priest and [that] of a secular thegn is reckoned equally valuable in English law, on account of the 7 church orders [through which the priest rises, lq] which the priest by God's grace was fortunate enough to receive (reckoned; and on account of … had, he is worthy [deemed worthy, Ld] of thegn-right, hlq).

Concerning the oath of ecclesiastics and concerning the compensation for offences against [those in] holy orders (Að and Hadbot) The oath of a mass-priest and a secular thegn is in the law of the English reckoned equally valuable, because of the seven orders of the Church which the priest, prospering through the grace of God, has obtained.

On Priests’ Oaths A priest’s oath and a secular thane’s are considered equal in English law; and because of the seven Church degrees that the priest has acquired through the grace of God, he is worthy of a thane’s rights.

The texts I include under this heading are those called by Liebermann Geþyncðo, Norðleoda laga, Mircna laga. Að and Hadbot, and printed by him, I, 456–69. Thorpe has the three first, in a different order, I, 186–93. The five texts occur in C.C.C.C., MS. 201, a manuscript with connections with Archbishop Wulfstan, and D.Bethurum has produced good reasons for assigning the collection to this prelate, who was deeply interested in this matter. The last three are also in C.C.C.C.. MS. 190, another manuscript connected with Wulfstan. All five, but not as a group or in order, are in the Textus Roffensis, and the authors of Quadripartitus and the Instituta Cnuti use them. Much of what is known of status in Anglo-Saxon times comes from these texts, which should not be regarded as official enactments but as a private compilation. [Her footnote 2: No. 52 in the 1955 edition] [Her footnote 3: Journ. Engl. and Germ. Phil., xlix, 449–63]

note.seg: Textus Roffensis adds: “he will be worthy of a thegn’s rights”.

Liebermann takes the first chapter of this with what precedes, i.e. (d), calling the two together Að. But MSS C.C.C.C. 201 and 190 have a new rubric, and go straight on to what Liebermann calls Hadbot. I keep their division. Textus Roffensis puts this first chapter, without rubric, before the text I call (d).
